## One connected expedition

1. Start New Game in isolated storage. Play the opening and prepare through reef/island exploration, food, tools, suit, reserves, recovery kit and paid Dart construction. Collect C01–C04 and the materials needed for the paid personal 350 m refit. Optional trim may be purchased, with its cost retained. Omit optional personal logs on the main route. Nothing may be spawned, teleported, granted or directly changed in saved state.
2. Read the preparation UI: actual suit and Dart limits, available ingredients, local fabrication and useful cargo. Refit the existing suit at its valid service site. Demonstrate that the Dart remains rated to 180 m. Take a conservative first Basin approach within that hull limit; exit only with adequate personal protection. Reach C05/C06 and collect useful Basin stock through actual interactions, including recognizable salvage and mineral hosts. Do not substitute only viewing a distant landmark for visiting the site.
3. Return by the connected intended route, store useful cargo and service at a valid refuge. Explain the concrete payoff and next regional lead without revealing later story meaning. Use the notebook and known-place markers through normal UI. Record what was legible from the first approach, where a stop/look/reorientation was needed, and any return friction.
4. Make a real local save, close/reload the page and Continue without reseeding. Compare the complete state against the exact production fixed-step replay for any elapsed idle input. Preserve equipment instance identity, paid recipes, stock, clues, damage/charge/cargo, refuge and recovery identities; distinguish wall-clock save metadata from gameplay state. Keep the source input trace outside page memory so reload cannot erase it.

Use ordinary keyboard/mouse/UI input. Deterministic event scheduling may assist measurement, but retain its timing and distinguish accelerated/controlled-frame diagnostics from continuous play. The first approach must be judged using on-screen regional leads, silhouettes, sources and warning cues; disclose any navigation that instead uses code coordinates or hidden state. Agent navigation is not fresh-human learning evidence. Retained earlier earned saves are useful comparisons, not a substitute for this new assembled-source route.

## Threat, geography and controls

OS2-06 remains open: an earlier level view at roughly 53 m showed water above the console while real cover was substantially below it. The prior warningApproach fixture proves quiet disengagement and a later cover maneuver, but does not prove that a player recognizes shelter during the earned first approach. Observe the actual route at level pitch and during deliberate looking. Preserve honest unfavorable views, detours and failures. Do not relabel quiet disengagement as cover, or assume historically named coverWest/labSheltered fixtures are sheltered.

Show warning before pursuit and an ordinary no-charge response: slow/quiet movement, retreat or reachable physical cover, with clear visual change and a real escape route. Record actual behind-cover/AI states separately from what the player sees. If shelter remains unreadable, return an earned pre-encounter save, ordinary input trace, exact views and a minimal proposed correction. Do not add a HUD paragraph or alter camera/geometry independently.

Inspect actual floor-contact and boarding routes after terrain correction, including rescue staging and Basin ledges. An earned contact/stall should retain the requested/actual movement, obstruction/support/surface result and presentation-reset reasons in a separate replay diagnostic. Keep OS3-03 unproven unless ordinary source evidence substantiates it; no threshold tuning based on seeded stalls. Verify meaningful bite feedback with sound muted/captions off in a clearly separated ordinary encounter continuation, preserving damage/disable/recovery priority.

Fork only from an unmodified exported checkpoint of this earned run on the same source. Through ordinary input, suffer a local failure/disabled Dart in the authored Basin route and demonstrate a viable starter-accessible recovery expedition. Knowledge, blueprints and essential tools must survive. Use actual local Bobbin initiation, complete tether route, tow/repair or salvage and cargo retrieval; no second duplicate advanced ship, unearned material grants, or remote story interaction. Preserve route identity through an actual mid-operation save/reload and complete the outcome. Verify the refuge/bench approach is both physically reachable and visually supported after the terrain correction.

Measure the cost and time of recovering, and what is irretrievably lost. A repeated-loss or alternate repair/salvage edge can be a separate labelled rule diagnostic where needed; do not present it as ordinary depletion/earned travel. If the failure route exposes a blocker, retain the complete before/after state and smallest actual reproduction rather than weakening validation or filtering the case.

Separate preparation, outward legs, site work and return. Measure oxygen/power immediately before every refill/service/entry, including the preceding minimum; the conservative intended route requires at least 25% remaining. Report travel versus collection/menu time, detours, collisions, failures and rescues honestly. Do not count paused wall time or controlled-frame duration as human playtime.

Retain useful motion around controls/threat/recovery, not only posed stills. Menus should use compact labels/costs with essential warnings; no repeated explanatory subtitles. Note cold/warm activation and obvious stalls on the actual route with hardware attribution; prior synthetic cache timings do not prove frame pacing.

Keep major narrative spoilers out of ordinary reports and media labels. Return one evidence commit, runnable reproduction commands, completion/defect table, limitations and clean resource release.
